There's something joyful about watching the cast throw everything at this production.

It’s also a little too hurried in places. Werner’s quick character switches – often without stepping away from the mic – are a highlight, and Stevens carries the story all the way to Christmas as wryly humorous, downtrodden George. There’s no question, by the end, that his is a wonderful life indeed.

Jessica Lazar’s atmospheric revival by the “Jermyn Street Theatre Radio Studio” delivers an impeccably executed celebration of the craft of radio-play-making, while paying strict homage to the source material and delivering laughs along the way.

Would adapting this cult classic for the stage prove as wonderful as its title suggests? Capra’s movie, which stars James Stewart as George Bailey, is perhaps much loved for its remarkable mix of fantasy, drama, humour and grief, and ultimately ends on a heartwarming note about the power of friendship and family.

Frank Capra movie It’s a Wonderful Life is often named as the greatest Christmas film of all time, though it was originally a flop before endearing itself to TV audiences as a festive staple over the last 50 years.

A family festive favourite that reminds us of all the good things about Christmas, of how it is better to give than receive, and reminds us that our dreams are sometimes under our very noses. It’s a Wonderful Life is a Christmas treat that finds itself happily landing at the Jermyn Street theatre until the New Year.
